questions.q: In the case study, why should Salesforce be configured as the SP rather than the IdP?
options: Salesforce cannot technically act as an SP
SAML only works when Salesforce is the IdP
Salesforce must always be the IdP in every workforce scenario
Entra ID is already the enterprise's IAM hub, and there's no indication any other app needs to launch from inside Salesforce
questions.explain: Since Entra ID is the existing hub and no other app needs to launch from Salesforce, Salesforce should be the SP, trusting Entra ID's authentication, per the hub-and-spoke reasoning from Lesson 14.

questions.q: Why is JIT provisioning alone not sufficient for this client's requirement that terminations reflect automatically in Salesforce access?
options: JIT only fires when a user attempts to log in, so a terminated employee who never logs in again triggers no JIT event to deactivate them
JIT provisioning is deprecated and unusable
Terminations are always instant regardless of provisioning method
JIT provisioning cannot be used with SAML
questions.explain: As covered in Lesson 12, JIT is a login-time mechanism only — it can't deactivate someone who simply stops logging in, which is exactly what happens after termination.

questions.q: What specific safeguard does the case study insist on before disabling the standard Salesforce login page broadly?
options: Removing all Connected Apps first
Nothing; it's always safe to disable it immediately after configuring SSO
Testing and keeping at least one admin profile able to use the standard login page as a break-glass path
Disabling MFA to simplify troubleshooting
questions.explain: Per Lesson 10's lockout warning, the case study insists on preserving a tested break-glass admin login path before broadly disabling standard login, in case the IdP has an outage.

questions.q: Why does the architect need to explicitly confirm MFA enforcement with the client's identity team, rather than assuming SSO implies it?
options: MFA is irrelevant once SSO is configured
MFA can only be enforced from within Salesforce, never from Entra ID
SSO always automatically implies MFA is enforced
Salesforce's own MFA requirement doesn't apply to SSO logins; the burden shifts to the external IdP, which must be separately verified to enforce MFA
questions.explain: As covered in Lesson 11, assuming SSO automatically means MFA is handled is a common and risky architectural mistake — it has to be explicitly verified on the IdP side.

questions.q: Per the case study, what is one of the three most common real-world failure points in a workforce SSO rollout?
options: A sloppy Federation ID mapping during a rushed go-live causing mismatched users
Enabling My Domain too early
Using too few OAuth scopes
Choosing SAML instead of OIDC
questions.explain: The case study names a sloppy Federation ID mapping during a rushed go-live (alongside an untested break-glass path and a deactivation gap in provisioning) as one of the three most common real-world failure points.
